specific_objectives: 7.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe the various types of propellers, principles of operation and pitch change mechanisms.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of CSU cutaway diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of a propeller in an aircraft?
How does a fixed pitch propeller differ from a variable pitch propeller?
Why is a constant speed propeller preferred for modern aircraft?

development.content:
Types of propellers
Fixed pitch vs Variable pitch
Constant speed unit components
Governor operation principles
Hydraulic pitch change mechanism

topics: Low speed and high speed stops
development.content:
CSU internal valve operation
Oil pressure and pitch relationship
Low speed and high speed stops
Blade angle adjustment logic
RPM maintenance during flight

Pitch change mechanisms
Hydraulic actuation systems
Feedback loops in CSU
Failure modes and indications
Maintenance considerations

summary_questions: Explain how the CSU maintains a constant RPM despite changes in engine power demand.
Describe the role of oil pressure in changing the propeller blade pitch.
What happens to the propeller pitch if the governor fails to maintain speed?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of CSU operation apply to the counteracting methods discussed in LP 05 regarding propeller rotation effects.

pft_rows.syllabus: Effect of propeller rotation on aircraft and methods used to counteract it
